name: voice-harness
description: Talk with a coding agent while it steers the editor and shows figures inline.

voiceHarness.nodePath.description: Absolute path to the node binary. Empty: resolve via a login shell.

voiceHarness.claudePath.description: Absolute path to the claude CLI. Empty: resolve via a login shell.

voiceHarness.voice.description: Kokoro voice for spoken replies (hear them all with tools/voice-sampler). Run Voice Harness: Restart Speech to apply.

voiceHarness.speakReplies.description: Whether replies are spoken when the panel opens (the 🔊 button toggles it).

voiceHarness.echoCancellation.description: Use macOS voice processing to cancel the speech echo, for use with speakers instead of headphones. Run Voice Harness: Restart Speech to apply.

voiceHarness.modelsDirectory.description: Folder for the speech models (downloaded on first use). Empty: ~/Library/Application Support/voice-harness/models. Run Voice Harness: Restart Speech to apply.

voiceHarness.autoInterrupt.description: Pause Claude's speech automatically when you start talking over it. Off: speech stops only when you press Talk or Stop. Run Voice Harness: Restart Speech to apply.

voiceHarness.sendEditorContext.description: Send the open file, visible lines, cursor line and selection with each message, so "this" and "here" refer to what you're looking at.

voiceHarness.conversationMode.description: Auto-listen when the panel opens: after Claude finishes a spoken reply, the mic opens for your answer and a pause sends it (the 🎧 button toggles it). Turns started with Talk still end with Done.

voiceHarness.location.description: Where Voice Harness: Open Panel puts the chat: the secondary sidebar, or an editor tab beside your code. Applies the next time the panel is opened.

enumDescriptions: Claude's answers in a reading serif (New York where available, otherwise Iowan Old Style or Georgia)
Claude's answers in the editor's interface font
voiceHarness.readingFont.description: Typeface for Claude's answers. The interface, code and your own messages always use VS Code's fonts.
